The transcript revisits the same three decision episodes in separate participant turns. These repeated manifestations are represented as separate eligible segments, while remaining one planned instance per bias for instance-level scoring.
The RAG output includes claimed source-passage excerpts but no independent retrieved chunks or retrieval logs, so citation fidelity cannot be verified.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I kept 2200 as my working target. I nudged it a little in my head, but I didn't sit down and recalculate from the new numbers.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant retained the handed-off 2200 target and made only a small adjustment despite learning the actual count and cycle conditions had changed. This is the primary manifestation of the single planned anchoring instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I could've recalculated from scratch ... Or radioed the hump conductor ... I didn't do either right away — I just carried the number forward.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a separate articulation of the same estimate-revision decision: the participant identifies recalculation and consultation as alternatives but carries the initial target forward. It is not an additional planned occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Probably if the discrepancy had been bigger ... if it'd been 50 cars ... Three extra cars didn't feel like enough to abandon the plan.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant describes a threshold for abandoning the initial target and treats the actual discrepancy as insufficient to do so. This is a repeated manifestation of the same planned anchoring instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: We'd had a derailment at this yard about three weeks earlier ... and that was fresh in my mind. I made the call to pull the whole eleven-car cut.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The recent derailment is explicitly connected to the choice to pull the full cut after a borderline alert. This is an initial articulation of the single planned availability-bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The derailment three weeks back was still sitting with me ... I didn't want a repeat, so I went bigger than the book probably called for.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The vivid recent event drives a response beyond standard procedure for the borderline reading. This repeats the same planned availability-bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: It didn't carry the same weight as the derailment ... even though logically the wet-weather false positives happen a lot more often.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant explicitly says the recalled derailment outweighed the more frequent wet-weather false positives. This is the clearest articulation of the planned availability-bias mechanism.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: One found a hairline mark ... The other inspected independently and cleared it ... There was also an old repair entry ... I ended up treating it as still suspect and asked for a third pass.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant describes treating the car as suspect after receiving both a mark and an independent clearance, while also mentioning the old repair entry. This is an initial articulation of the single planned confirmation-bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I leaned toward Carman A's finding ... Between the mark and that history, it felt like enough to keep the car flagged. I asked for a third inspection rather than accepting Carman B's clearance.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant favors evidence supporting suspicion and rejects the independent clearance, using the old unrelated repair entry as supporting context. This repeats the same planned confirmation-bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Once I already suspected the car, the mark and the repair history just fit what I expected to find. Carman B's 'all clear' almost read to me like it needed double-checking.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant directly describes a prior suspicion shaping interpretation of supporting evidence and discounting a procedurally equivalent clearance. This is the clearest articulation of the planned confirmation-bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: If Carman B's report had come in first ... I might have closed it out right there. Order mattered more than it should have, probably.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a retrospective counterfactual about report order. The hidden manifest contains no primacy-effect instance, and this statement does not establish the defined confirmation-bias mechanism of selectively weighting evidence according to a prior defect hypothesis.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I set the car out and dispatched the rest of the train. Holding the whole consist for one car wasn't going to help anyone ... we'd only eat a partial penalty instead of a full one.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The specification explicitly designates this as a genuine trade-off under competing constraints rather than a biased inference. The participant weighs the unresolved car against the SLA consequences of holding the consist.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: If the derailment three weeks earlier had never happened ... I think I isolate just the one car and keep moving.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a retrospective counterfactual, not an additional decision-time manifestation. The planned availability instance is mapped to the actual sensor-risk decision and its contemporaneous reasoning.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I'd probably push back harder on the initial time estimate instead of just carrying it forward.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a proposed future correction during retrospective reflection, not a separate manifested bias occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I'd try to look at both carmen's reports side by side instead of one at a time.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a proposed future method for reviewing reports, not a separate manifested bias occurrence.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 1: retaining or recalculating the 2200 classification-completion target after the actual count and retarder pace differed from the handoff.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Insufficient adjustment away from the handed-off 2200/38-car estimate despite materially different new information: 41 cars and slower retarder cycling.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Anchoring and adjustment is an established name for the anchoring mechanism, and the finding describes insufficient adjustment from the initial target after new information.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The RAG identifies the handed-off 2200 target as a reference point, the new car count and slower cycle time, and the participant's small rather than full recalculation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted statements about keeping 2200 and treating three extra cars as insufficient to abandon the plan are present in the interview and attributed to the participant.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 2: choosing whether to isolate GATX 88213 or pull the full eleven-car cut after a borderline hot-box reading.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: A vivid recent derailment disproportionately inflates the perceived risk of a borderline detector reading and outweighs the known wet-weather false-positive history.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Availability heuristic is an established alternate label for availability bias, and the stated mechanism is the same construct.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding captures the vivid recent derailment, the borderline reading, the underweighted wet-weather false-positive history, and the resulting oversized inspection response.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The cited statements about the recent derailment, the full-cut inspection, and the greater frequency of false positives appear in the interview and are attributed to the participant.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 3: weighing Carman A's hairline-mark report and Carman B's independent clearance for GATX 88213.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: After suspecting a defect, the participant treats ambiguous supporting evidence and an unrelated closed repair entry as confirmation while discounting a procedurally equivalent clearance.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The predicted label exactly matches the hidden target label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding describes the pre-existing suspicion, the supporting mark and old repair entry, and the discounting of Carman B's equally credible all-clear.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted statements about leaning toward Carman A, using the old repair entry, and treating Carman B's report as needing double-checking appear in the interview.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: The quote is valid and concerns the same inspection episode, but a possible report-order effect is a different construct from the hidden confirmation-bias mechanism. It does not establish selective weighting of evidence according to the pre-existing defect hypothesis, and the hidden manifest contains no primacy-effect instance.

candidates.details: The participant's order counterfactual supports a possible report-order effect, but the hidden target at this episode is confirmation bias based on selective evidence weighting. The candidate adds a false alarm on a negative segment and does not add an instance-level true positive.

high_only.detection_interpretation: The high-only finding detects the confirmation-bias segment. The two moderate-confidence findings are excluded, leaving eight of nine positive repeated-expression segments undetected.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: All three hidden instances are detected at their primary mapped segments, with no false alarms. Repeated articulations of the same instances remain separate positive segments under the span-based map.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: The result is unchanged from high_and_moderate because the RAG output contains no low-confidence identified findings.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: The candidate adds a false alarm on the report-order counterfactual segment without detecting an additional hidden instance.

rag_label_false_positive_inventory.mechanism_overlap_summary: The candidate and hidden confirmation-bias instance concern the same conflicting-report episode and both involve evidence weighting, but the candidate attributes the decision to report order while the hidden mechanism is selective weighting based on an existing defect hypothesis.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: Adds two moderate-confidence true positives, raising strict and mechanism-first instance F1 from 0.5000 to 1.0000 and segment hits from 1 to 3.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: No change; the RAG output contains no low-confidence identified findings.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: The candidate adds no instance true positive and adds one false positive in both instance scorecards plus one segment-level false alarm; instance F1 falls from 1.0000 to 0.8571.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, all three mapped primary bias segments are detected without false alarms. The span-level map also contains repeated manifestations of the same decisions, so six repeated-expression segments remain misses.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: All three hidden instances are correctly identified with full mechanisms and valid evidence at high_and_moderate and all_identified_confidence_levels. At high_only, the two moderate findings are missed.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: Matches the strict scorecard at every threshold because the two non-exact labels are established equivalents and all three mechanisms are fully captured.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The primacy-effect candidate is a plausible, interview-supported near miss, but it is a different construct from the hidden confirmation-bias mechanism. Including candidates adds a false alarm and no true positive.
main_failure_modes: Anchoring and availability findings are only moderate confidence, so both are missed at the high-only threshold.
The primacy-effect candidate treats a report-order counterfactual as a separate bias prediction despite no matching hidden instance.
main_strengths: All three planned bias instances are identified at the recommended high_and_moderate threshold.
Each identified finding gives a full mechanism account and uses valid interview evidence.
The RAG distinguishes the genuinely constrained dispatch trade-off from the biased reasoning episodes.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: The identified-occurrence tier performs perfectly at the instance level when moderate confidence is included. Candidate inclusion reduces precision without adding recall. Segment-level performance is lower because the transcript separately revisits and manifests the same three planned decision instances across multiple eligible spans.
